_why: On the owner's real library 07-27 and 07-30 are BOTH import days and lit days, so a gate of the form 'the trace renders on at least one page' PASSES TODAY under the superseded design and is degenerate; this fixture's import days and blessing days do not intersect at all, so a gate built on it cannot pass by accident.
_shape: Days are stored as [year, month, day, hour] and converted by the test with the shipped local-noon idiom (new Date(y, m-1, d, h)), NEVER as epoch ms: a hardcoded epoch would name a different local calendar day in a different machine timezone, which is the one thing every day-bucketing assertion in this suite depends on.
_synthetic: Contains no real data. Every id, title, folder and body here is invented for this file. The owner's library is neither read nor written by anything that uses it.

zero_overlap._disjointness: import days {07/19, 07/26, 07/15} and blessing days {07/30, 06/03} share nothing. The test asserts this property itself, because a later edit could quietly reintroduce an overlap and hollow out every gate built on the fixture.

adjacency._why: A day that is BOTH an import day and a lit day, kept in its OWN section so the zero-overlap section above stays genuinely zero-overlap. Two of the owner's seven real import days are exactly this, so the collapse-to-one-entry case is driven over a fixture that contains one rather than reasoned about.

blessings.why: welcomed on the day it arrived
